heading: INT. TIDAL STATION KARST-9, CONTROL DECK - NIGHT

units.text: INT. TIDAL STATION KARST-9, CONTROL DECK - NIGHT
Emergency red.
Sea slams the hull in slow, enormous beats.
Consoles flicker.
VESNA DRAGOVIC, 40s, flight engineer, drags a sparking panel off its mount.
AMARA OKORO, 30s, station medic, hangs from a ceiling rail with a pressure kit.
Hull's breached on four. How long?
units.name: VESNA

units.text: Ninety seconds, maybe. Maybe less.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: She hits her harness release and drops.
Vesna catches her by the arm, then lets go quickly, as if burned.
Don't touch the wet floor. It's live.
units.name: VESNA

units.text: Then why are you standing in it?
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Because she's the only one who can reach the valve.
units.name: VESNA

units.text: Which she?
Neither answers.
They both look at the valve wheel, high on the wall, and then at each other.
She waits for the other to move.
Breathe. Count. Move.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Do it!
units.name: VESNA

units.text: Amara climbs the rack.
Vesna steadies the base, jaw tight.
The lights die.
Only the emergency strip shows, a thin red seam.
Anyone still on the station, brace! Brace now!
units.name: VESNA

units.text: Silence.
Water on steel.
Nobody's here, Vesna. It's just us.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: A heavy clunk.
The wheel turns.
The sea's rhythm slows, then stops.
Lights stutter back on.
Amara hangs from the wheel, laughing without sound.
She did it. I can't believe she did it.
units.name: VESNA

units.text: I'm right here.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: I know.
units.name: VESNA

units.text: The wall behind them splits along a seam, and seawater sheets down, blank and cold.
They stop laughing.
That's six.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Then we swim.
units.name: VESNA
